solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Join a friend touring holiday destination, ignoring one area

indicators.note: a friend touring a place goes round it, so the words for a friend wrap around the place

parts.note: a mate is a friend

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out, so a letter is dropped from the resort

parts.note: Malaga is a Spanish resort on the Costa del Sol
A is the standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Someone joins a pal on a tour of a sunny resort, skipping one part of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one of the resort's two A's goes under 'ignoring'; 'touring' has the pal's letters go round what remains, so the answer opens with the clue's own 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: To amalgamate things is to merge or combine them into one, a synonym of join.

clue.text: Friend's friendly when losing power

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away, so a letter goes from the adjective

parts.note: pally is informal for friendly
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A friend stays friendly only until they lose their influence.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Friend stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is someone on your side, a supporter or friend.

clue.text: Pull dustcart taking back bottles

indicators.note: taking back means the run of letters is read in the opposite direction
bottles here is a verb: the phrase holds the letters inside it like a bottle

explanation.surface: A rubbish lorry hauls away a load of returned empty bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' tells you the answer is held within 'dustcart taking'; 'back' says it runs right to left there.
explanation.definitionFit: To attract is to draw something towards you, as a magnet does: to pull.

clue.text: Get to catch throw by one who's terrible ball player

indicators.note: by means next to, so the next piece follows on
to catch something is to hold it, so the verb's letters enclose the throw

parts.note: taken as written
a lob is a high throw
a rotter is a dreadful, nasty person

explanation.surface: A bad sportsman is urged to catch a throw.
explanation.walkthrough: The Harlem Globetrotters are an American exhibition basketball team.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Harlem Globetrotters basketball team is a ball player.

clue.text: One who might shoot king arrested by alien?

indicators.note: arrested means held, so the alien holds the king inside

parts.note: a Martian, or Mars man, is a stock alien
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A monarch taken into custody by a visitor from space wonders whether it will shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A marksman is a skilled shot with a rifle or pistol.

clue.text: The best setter

definitions.meaning: the person in charge or the winner, the one on top
a setter is a breed of gundog, and the crossword setter puts himself at the top of the tree

explanation.surface: The setter claims to be the finest.
explanation.definitionFit: A top dog is the leader or champion, and a setter is a dog, playfully a superior one.

clue.text: Gloom ultimately surrounding 3?

parts.note: fog is murk or gloom

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Murk closes in on the clue three entries away.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference: 3 down is GLOBETROTTER, and Phileas Fogg of Around the World in Eighty Days is a famous one.
explanation.definitionFit: Jules Verne's Phileas Fogg circled the world in eighty days, the archetypal world traveller.

clue.text: Public housing unlimited near gorge

indicators.note: housing means holding inside, so one word goes into the other

parts.note: overt means open or public

indicators.note: without its limits, the word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A public housing scheme without boundaries sits beside a gorge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gorge' looks like a ravine but it is the verb: to eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To gorge is to stuff yourself with food, eating far too much.

clue.text: Shiny rubbish bins discovered to contain goods? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one piece goes round the other
this reverses the containment the surface describes, so the goods hold the rest

parts.note: G is short for good, so goods gives two of them
litter is rubbish

indicators.note: dis-covered, its cover taken off, so the word loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: Bright bins full of rubbish are meant to hold merchandise, but it is the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' takes the outer letters off 'bins' for IN. 'Quite the opposite' flips the containment: G and G wrap LITTERIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Glittering means sparkling or gleaming brightly, so it is a synonym of shiny.

clue.text: Print of house with illuminated table outside

indicators.note: the illuminated table goes outside the house, wrapping it

parts.note: lit means illuminated
a graph is a chart or table of data

explanation.surface: A picture of a home, with a lamp-lit table standing outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A lithograph is a print made from a flat stone or metal plate.

clue.text: Angry over Republican leaving shop

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters are read backwards
leaving means going away, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: riled means annoyed, angry

explanation.surface: A furious Republican storms out of a store.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling cooked meats and fine foods.

clue.text: Quickly leave after defeat yet to be arranged

indicators.note: after puts the word for leave at the end

parts.note: to lick an opponent is to beat them

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the word's letters are shuffled

parts.note: to split is slang for to leave

explanation.surface: Someone means to quit promptly once a loss, not yet sorted, is dealt with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be arranged' shuffles YET into ETY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lickety-split is an informal American phrase meaning at great speed, very fast.

clue.text: Shake stage when speaking

indicators.note: when spoken the word sounds like the one in the grid

parts.note: a phase is a stage in a process

explanation.surface: Nerves before speaking on a stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage' suggests a theatre, but it is a step in a process.
explanation.definitionFit: To faze someone is to unsettle or disconcert them, to shake them.

clue.text: Doctor so stilted and most unemotional

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with or alter, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wooden, stiff physician is the coolest customer of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a physician but is a verb ordering the letters of 'so stilted' to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Stolid means impassive and showing little feeling; the superlative is least emotional.

clue.text: Tenacious relative runs up surrounded by exercise books

indicators.note: the letters for exercise and books sit on either side, enclosing the rest

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

indicators.note: in a down entry up means towards the top, so the letter moves to the front

parts.note: a sister is a relative
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A dogged family member dashes about between PE kit and textbooks.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'up' means towards the top, so 'runs up' lifts the relative's R to the front before the exercise books wrap round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Persistent means refusing to give up, holding on firmly, which is tenacious.

clue.text: Lasting kiss inside … and outside

indicators.note: inside means the kiss goes within the word for lasting

parts.note: eternal means everlasting
X is the conventional written kiss

explanation.surface: An everlasting kiss indoors, and then out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays 'inside' against 'outside': the first is the containment signal, the second the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: External means on the outer side, relating to the outside.

clue.text: Cousins maybe ask about time with Queen

indicators.note: with means alongside, so the Queen's letters join on
about signals moving the letters around into a new order

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Royal relatives ask the Queen about the time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cousins' is not family: Robin Cousins is a British figure skater who won Olympic gold in 1980.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Cousins was an Olympic champion on ice, so he is an example of a figure skater.

clue.text: Outdoor air that could benefit a lady?

definitions.text: Outdoor air that could benefit a lady?

parts.words: Outdoor air that could benefit a lady?
parts.note: 'air' sounds like fresh air but means a tune, sung outside a window to a woman being courted

explanation.surface: Fresh air would do a woman good.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is a song performed at night by a suitor outside his beloved's window.

clue.text: Protection from cooking fat? Yes

indicators.note: cooking the books is falsifying them, so the letters are cooked into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook asks whether a guard against frying fat is needed, and is told yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Safety is the condition of being protected from danger or harm.

clue.text: Force fighting in splinter group

parts.note: F is the physics abbreviation for force
action is military combat, fighting

explanation.surface: Violent fighting breaks out within a breakaway cell.
explanation.definitionFit: A faction is a small dissenting group within a larger party.

clue.text: Plane? No, it's undergoing repair in shed

parts.note: a jet is a plane

indicators.note: repair puts things back together, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A plane stands in a hangar being fixed, or so we think.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like the building but it is the verb: to cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw away or discard, as cargo is dumped from a ship.

clue.text: Shuffle last of cards hard, then proceed at leisure

indicators.note: then means next, so the following piece comes afterwards
last of takes only the final letter of the word

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
to amble is to walk at a leisurely pace

explanation.surface: A card player mixes the deck vigorously and then takes their time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shuffle' sits by 'cards' to suggest a deck, but it is a way of walking.
explanation.definitionFit: To shamble is to walk awkwardly, dragging the feet, which is to shuffle.

clue.text: Bear with pub having cider only now and then

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: only now and then picks out alternate letters of the word

explanation.surface: A bear in a bar orders cider just occasionally.
explanation.definitionFit: Winnie-the-Pooh, A A Milne's honey-loving teddy, is a famous bear.

clue.text: Close drip, stopping leak

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a hole, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: to secrete is to discharge or ooze, to leak
IV is an intravenous drip

explanation.surface: A plumber shuts off a drip to stop a leak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like the verb to shut but is the adjective, pronounced to rhyme with 'dose'. IV is a hospital drip.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone close is reticent and keeps things to themselves, as a secretive person does.

clue.text: Control southern route

parts.note: a way is a route

explanation.surface: Someone takes charge of the road going south.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold sway is to have power or influence over others.

clue.text: Place to eat pickle

definitions.meaning: a dining room for soldiers or officers in the armed forces
a predicament or muddle, a tight spot

explanation.surface: Somewhere to dine on preserved vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is a forces dining hall, and also a muddle or predicament.

clue.text: Film with prince initially usurping king in Morecambe?

indicators.note: usurping means taking another's place, so one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: Eric Morecambe was half of the British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise
R is short for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A movie in which a prince seizes the throne, set in a Lancashire seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe is also a Lancashire resort, but here it is the comedian Eric Morecambe.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long film on a grand, heroic scale.

clue.text: In story, returning evil's held to be perfect

indicators.note: held means kept inside, so the reversed word sits within the story

parts.note: a fable is a moral tale or story

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: ill can mean evil or harm

explanation.surface: In a tale the wicked return but are judged flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'evil's' stands for 'is', and 'to be' is a link; 'returning' turns the evil backwards before 'held' sets it in the story.
explanation.definitionFit: Infallible means incapable of error, without fault, which is perfect.

clue.text: For this song might make fortune

indicators.note: the first word plus the answer might make the last word, so taking that first word away leaves the answer

explanation.surface: A song that could bring its singer riches.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'FOR + this might make fortune': take FOR from the front of 'fortune' and what is left is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune is a melody, the musical part of a song.

clue.text: Unyielding regarding missing holy period?

parts.note: re means regarding, concerning
Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter
the suffix -less means without, missing

explanation.surface: An inflexible person on the subject of skipping a religious season.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are not in clue order: LENT-LESS means 'missing Lent'.
explanation.definitionFit: Relentless means not giving up or easing off, unyielding.
